## 9-Zone Directional & Ordered Control Dock (`add_control`)

In `leaflet`, placing multiple controls, legends, or toolbars in the same corner often causes them to overlap. `glmap` introduces a **9-zone directional layout grid** (`x = left | center | right`, `y = top | center | bottom`) inside an isolated CSS stacking context (`isolation: isolate; z-index: 0;`):

- `"top-left"`, `"top-center"`, `"top-right"`
- `"center-left"`, `"center-center"`, `"center-right"`
- `"bottom-left"`, `"bottom-center"`, `"bottom-right"`

Each zone stacks its child widgets in a configurable `direction` (`"vertical"` or `"horizontal"`) sorted by numeric `order`, while automatically reserving space for the bottom-left scale bar and bottom-right copyright attribution:

```{r}
library(glmap)

glmap(basemap = "dark") |>
  add_search_osm(position = "top-left", order = 5) |>
  add_layers_control(
    baseGroups = c("Dark", "Light", "Satellite"),
    overlayGroups = c("Risks", "Claims"),
    position = "top-left",
    options = layers_control_options(collapsed = TRUE),
    order = 10
  ) |>
  add_draw_toolbar(position = "bottom-left", direction = "vertical", order = 15) |>
  add_measure(position = "bottom-right", order = 15) |>
  add_minimap(position = "bottom-right", width = 140, height = 110, order = 80)
```

---

## Interactive Vector Draw Toolbar (`add_draw_toolbar`), Measure (`add_measure`) & OSM Search (`add_search_osm`)

- **`add_draw_toolbar()`**: Draw **Polygons** (click vertices, double-click or click first vertex to close), **Rectangles** (click-drag), **Geodesic Circles** (click center, drag radius in meters), **Polylines**, and **Markers**. Clicking a completed shape opens a popup with a **Remove** button, or click **Clear** to remove all drawn shapes.
- **`add_measure()`**: Click points on the map to measure geodesic path distance (`m` / `km`) and spherical-excess polygon area (`sq. m` / `sq. km`).
- **`add_search_osm()`**: Live geocoding search bar powered by OpenStreetMap Nominatim.
- **`add_graticule()` & `add_terminator()`**: Add coordinate meridians/parallels and the real-time solar day/night hemisphere polygon.

## Show/Hide Layer Groups & Zero-Copy Shiny Proxy (`glmap_proxy`)

In Shiny applications, use `glmapOutput()`, `renderGlmap()`, and `glmap_proxy()` (or their drop-in aliases `leafletOutput()`, `renderLeaflet()`, and `leafletProxy()`) to update layers, toggle groups, or change GPU raster shader uniforms in **0 ms** without re-rendering the map widget:

```{r, eval = FALSE}
library(shiny)
library(glmap)

bench <- gl_benchmark_data(n_points = 50000L, raster_dim = c(200L, 200L))

ui <- fluidPage(
  fluidRow(
    column(3,
      selectInput("pal", "GPU Raster Palette", c("terrain", "viridis", "magma", "turbo", "rdylbu")),
      checkboxInput("hill", "Real-Time GPU Hillshade", TRUE),
      sliderInput("op", "Raster Opacity", 0, 1, 0.75, step = 0.05),
      selectInput("mode", "Marker Engine", c("auto", "cluster", "lod", "atlas", "points"))
    ),
    column(9,
      glmapOutput("map", height = "620px")
    )
  )
)

server <- function(input, output, session) {
  output$map <- renderGlmap({
    glmap(basemap = "dark") |>
      add_raster(bench$raster_mat, id = "dem", group = "DEM", palette = "terrain", hillshade = TRUE) |>
      add_points(bench$points_df, id = "pts", group = "Sensors", color = ~intensity, palette = "turbo") |>
      add_draw_toolbar(position = "bottom-left") |>
      add_measure(position = "bottom-right")
  })

  # 0ms GPU uniform update — does NOT re-transfer the Float32 raster!
  observe({
    glmap_proxy("map") |>
      set_raster_style("dem", palette = input$pal, hillshade = input$hill, opacity = input$op)
  })

  # 0ms Marker rendering mode switch
  observeEvent(input$mode, {
    glmap_proxy("map") |>
      set_marker_mode("pts", mode = input$mode)
  }, ignoreInit = TRUE)
}
```

## Exporting Standalone HTML (`gl_save_html`) & Static PNG / PDF (`gl_save_png`)

Both the MapLibre GL base canvas and the WebGL2 overlay canvas are initialized with `preserveDrawingBuffer: true`, so Quarto HTML/PDF reports and `gl_save_png()` capture crisp, full-resolution GPU renders:

```{r, eval = FALSE}
m <- glmap(bench$points_df, basemap = "dark") |>
  add_points(color = ~intensity, palette = "turbo")

# Save interactive HTML
gl_save_html(m, "map.html", selfcontained = TRUE)

# Capture high-DPI static PNG via headless Chromium (chromote)
gl_save_png(m, "map.png", vwidth = 1200, vheight = 750)
```
